source: Source: U.S. Dept. of Transportation, "Bumping & Oversales"

scenes.text: Airlines sell more tickets than the plane has seats. And it's legal.
scenes.head: MORE TICKETS THAN SEATS

scenes.text: The U.S. Department of Transportation says so. Airlines bet somebody won't show up.
scenes.head: THEY BET ON NO-SHOWS

scenes.text: Everybody shows up? First, they ask for volunteers.
scenes.head: FIRST: VOLUNTEERS

scenes.text: Bumped anyway? You can be owed four times your one-way fare. Up to $2,150.
scenes.say: Bumped anyway? You can be owed four times your one-way fare. Up to twenty-one hundred fifty dollars.
scenes.head: UP TO 4x YOUR FARE

scenes.text: So... take the cash, or keep your seat?
scenes.head: CASH OR SEAT?

scenes.text: Remember that at the gate, because...
scenes.head: REMEMBER THIS
